faultHelp.SHORT_CIRCUIT: The current found a path straight from one side of the battery to the other with nothing to slow it down, so it rushed through and blew the fuse. Put a load in that path, such as an LED bulb with a resistor, or a motor.
faultHelp.OVERCURRENT: There is more current in this path than the parts can carry safely. Raise the resistance by adding a resistor, or turn the supply voltage down.
faultHelp.REVERSED_POLARITY: A component is connected the wrong way round, so it blocks the current instead of using it. Swap its two ends and try again.
faultHelp.SINGULAR_SYSTEM: This circuit has no single answer the simulator can work out, usually because a part is wired across itself. Remove the connection that joins a component's two terminals together.

1.name: Easy
1.summary: Learn the basics: closed loops and switches. The rover shows what is on and what is off.
1.disclosure: No numbers, just parts that are lit or dark.

2.name: Medium
2.disclosure: Brightness bars that compare parts, with no units.

3.name: Hard
3.summary: Power the whole rover and recover from a short circuit.

4.name: Super Hard
4.summary: Control current with resistors and change the supply voltage.
4.disclosure: Everything: volts, ohms, amps and totals.

cb-01-closed-circuit.title: Close the loop
cb-01-closed-circuit.hint: Join the battery, the resistor and the LED bulb in a ring, and bring a wire back to the battery. If the bulb stays dark, check which way round it is connected.
cb-01-closed-circuit.learn: Current only flows around a closed loop. The resistor protects the LED bulb from too much current.

cb-02-switch-control.title: Switch it on
cb-02-switch-control.goal: Light the headlight with the switch closed, then turn it off and on again.
cb-02-switch-control.hint: The switch is already on the board. Put it in the loop with the battery, the resistor and the LED bulb, then select it to open or close it.
cb-02-switch-control.learn: A switch opens or closes the loop. When it is open the loop is cut, no current flows and the light goes out.

cb-03-series-loop.title: One loop for two
cb-03-series-loop.goal: Light the headlight and sound the buzzer in the same loop.
cb-03-series-loop.hint: Put the LED bulb and the buzzer one after the other in the same loop, with the resistor and the switch. Then open the switch and watch both.
cb-03-series-loop.learn: In a series circuit the same current goes through every part, one after the other. Open the switch and everything stops.

cb-04-parallel-branches.title: Two paths
cb-04-parallel-branches.goal: Give the headlight one path and the buzzer another, each with its own switch.
cb-04-parallel-branches.hint: Connect both paths to the same battery terminals. Each path has its own switch. Open one and see what the other does.
cb-04-parallel-branches.learn: In a parallel circuit each path is its own loop. Switching one off leaves the other running.

cb-05-series-vs-parallel.title: Power the whole rover
cb-05-series-vs-parallel.goal: Run the motors, the headlight and the buzzer at the same time.
cb-05-series-vs-parallel.hint: Wire the parts side by side, each one straight across the battery, with the resistor in front of the LED bulb. Motors in one series loop turn very slowly.
cb-05-series-vs-parallel.learn: Parts side by side each get the full battery voltage. Parts in series share it, so motors in series get less and turn more slowly.

cb-06-short-circuit-recovery.title: Beat the short circuit
cb-06-short-circuit-recovery.goal: Light the headlight even if a short circuit blows the fuse first.
cb-06-short-circuit-recovery.hint: A wire straight across the battery blows the fuse. Reset the fuse, take that wire away and put the load back in the loop.
cb-06-short-circuit-recovery.learn: A path with almost no resistance lets a huge current through. Always keep a load in the loop, and reset the fuse once the fault is fixed.

cb-07-resistance-limits-current.title: Tame the current
cb-07-resistance-limits-current.goal: Light the LED with a safe current, using the battery and LED already on the board.
cb-07-resistance-limits-current.hint: Put a resistor in series with the LED. Two resistors in series add up. Two in parallel give less resistance than one, so more current flows.
cb-07-resistance-limits-current.learn: Current is voltage divided by resistance. More resistance means less current, and resistors in parallel lower the total resistance.

cb-08-variable-voltage.title: Find the right voltage
cb-08-variable-voltage.goal: Power the motor, the buzzer and the headlight from one battery, and find which supply voltages work.
cb-08-variable-voltage.hint: Close the master switch and the headlight switch. Change the supply voltage with the slider: the motor needs enough voltage to turn, and the LED can get too much current if it is high.
cb-08-variable-voltage.learn: Voltage pushes current through resistance. If it is too low the motor will not turn. If it is too high the LED carries more current than it is rated for.
